title: Input rewind after a return
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, let $D$ be a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes, and let $x$ be a Boolean input. Suppose the call specification at node $l$ is $cs$. Starting from the compiled machine in its second return phase at $l$, with segment index $s$, direction bit $dir$, result bit $b$, arbitrary register and decider tapes, head positions, and output, take an input-head position $ip$ whose value is $j$, where $j\le |x|$. Through every time $t\le j+1$, all work-tape head positions remain unchanged; after $j+1$ steps the configuration has input-head position $1$, the same tapes, work-head positions and output, and state given by the return successor determined by $cs,l,s,dir,b$ and register index $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $l$ is a node and $cs$ is its call specification: $P.call(l)=some\ cs$
